title: Choose Gapl's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Scoreboard Chase. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Scoreboard Chase
options.lineage: Hand-hung stadium scoreboards and Indian TV cricket data graphics (Manhattan, worm, DRS screen)
options.thesis: Your application as a run chase: the verdict on the big screen, the gap as runs required, the roadmap as overs.
options.viewport: A painted scoreboard fills the first screen. Huge condensed tiles read READINESS 65 · NEEDS 13 · OFF 3 WEEKS, a DRS-style panel shows the Reject verdict with its reason, and a working role + tier picker with Analyze sits in the board's bottom rail.
options.risk: Cricket can tip into costume and puns, so copy stays literal and keeps the product's own words (Shortlist / Maybe / Reject). A student who doesn't follow cricket still has to read it plainly.

raised.raise: Every number carries a leader line to the reason behind it: each readiness component points at the gap pulling it down.
Verdict states read without color: the word, a pattern band and a position, never red/green alone.
One giant numeral per viewport. Hierarchy comes from extreme scale contrast, not boxes.
Total color commitment: the green field owns whole sections, with no grey-template sections between them.
One control drives the whole board: picking a tier re-flips every tile live.
Roadmap state is a scorebook mark, not a hue: a tick for done, a dot for untouched, a flag where you stopped.

options.label: PNR Status
options.lineage: Indian Railways reservation charts, PNR enquiry and station LED boards
options.thesis: Readiness as reservation status: waitlisted → RAC → confirmed, and the chart tells you what moves you up.
options.viewport: A coach reservation chart with your row highlighted: the status column shows Reject as WL 12, the reason printed as a remark, and an amber LED strip scrolling the next build.
options.risk: The most instantly legible metaphor for this audience, and also the one most runs would reach for. It also carries waitlist anxiety.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.lineage: Film editing bench, select rail and trim bin
options.thesis: Roadmap weeks as frames on a rail, with a flag where you stopped.
options.viewport: A perforated rail of weeks across an orange field.
options.case: Fits the roadmap, but students don't recognise film editing and the verdict gets lost.
options.kept: State is a mark, not a hue.
options.risk: Reads as a film tool, not a career tool.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: One slider morphs the whole page.
options.viewport: A giant numeral that changes as you drag.
options.case: Students don't identify with it, and the verdict becomes a typographic toy.
options.kept: One control drives the whole board.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Scores as forces you can trace.
options.case: Too abstract for a student at 1am, and loses on clarity.
options.kept: Every number is traceable to its cause.

options.label: Silk Canopy Chords
options.viewport: Crossing silk lanes over a bright field.
options.case: Beautiful, but says nothing about rejection or projects.

options.label: Brodovitch Spread
options.viewport: Pose on the left, answer on the right.
options.case: Luxury fashion language is foreign to placement-season students.

options.label: Highlife Sleeve
options.viewport: Arched hand-brushed name over mango and palm.
options.case: Festive tone fights the honest-verdict voice.
options.risk: Celebratory where the product is sober.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light SaaS page with a sample report card, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and CTA on the left, a sample report on the right, sections of feature rows below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Jobscan / Resume Worded by design.
